rows: Hay barn reported blown two hundred yards by the high winds at County Road 9 and Farm to Market Road 1046.

An old barn was reported blown down by the high winds.

Metal building roof caved in and windows and doors were blown out by the high winds. Two houses had their roof raised and several trees with eight inch diameter limbs were blown down. No injuries were reported.
Whole cottonwood trees were blown over by the high winds. Powerlines and power poles were blown down. Overhead doors blown out of a barn. No injuries were reported.

Reported on the Hemphill County and Wheeler County line.

The thunderstorm wind gusts caused multiple horse trailers to be flipped over as relayed by the National Severe Storms Laboratory. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
The thunderstorm wind gusts caused damage to a center pivot system. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
The hail was reported by the Texas Department of Public Safety on Interstate 40 in the town of Shamrock, Texas.

The public estimated hailstones the size of golf balls 7 miles northeast of Gageby. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement received golf ball size hail 5 miles east-northeast of Shamrock, Texas.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail 5 miles east of Mobeetie.
